summary: Luo's sense-selection model for simple homonymy by overloading in coercive subtyping (Chatzikyriakidis & Luo 2020 §3.3.2, code = the book's own Appendix A7.2, transcribed verbatim): the homonym 'run' as the unit type Onerun with one constructor, two meanings run1 : Human->Prop and run2 : Human->Institution->Prop, and two Coq Coercions r1/r2 playing c1/c2 of the book's Figure 3.1; the worked examples 'John runs quickly' (3.34) and 'John runs a bank' (3.35) are Definitions whose successful elaboration IS the automated disambiguation — the type ascriptions (run:T1)/(run:T2) trigger the correct coercion. 19 lines, zero theorems: the book's headline equations (3.39)-(3.40) are never stated, though the audit confirmed both close by reflexivity over signature-only assumptions.

sources.citation: Chatzikyriakidis, S. & Luo, Z. (2020). Formal Semantics in Modern Type Theories. Wiley/ISTE. §3.3.2 (homonymy and overloading, eqs. 3.34-3.40, Figure 3.1) and Appendix A7.2 (the Coq code this file transcribes).
Luo, Z. (2011b). Contextual analysis of word meanings in type-theoretical semantics. LACL 2011, LNAI 6736. (Original proposal of the overloading treatment; content reproduced in the 2020 book.)

determination_rationale: The formalization IS the source's own Coq code, and it compiles: the successful elaboration of (run:T1)/(run:T2) is precisely the 'automated selection of the correct meaning' the theory claims, and the audit confirmed the two headline equations (3.39)-(3.40) hold by definitional equality (reflexivity, signature-only assumptions) — no simplification, no extra assumption, no restructuring. Caveats recorded rather than counted against the theory: the file itself states zero theorems (a two-line Qed upgrade would make this a self-contained determination-1 record), Coq's elaborator coercions simulate rather than implement coercive subtyping (no coherence checking; ascriptions trigger selection) — class (iv), the rubric's named example of missing native structure — and the source's own CN := Set is a class (ii) collapse.

artifact_classes.description: Coercive subtyping is not native to Coq: the elaborator's Coercion mechanism simulates it without the theory's coherence condition, and sense selection must be triggered by explicit ascriptions (run:T1)/(run:T2) instead of the bare contextual typing requirement of Luo's calculus
CN := Set (inherited from Coq_book_ontology): the MTT universe of common nouns is collapsed onto a Coq universe, so every Set counts as a CN — the source's own implementation choice
